questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That my boyfriend lived in Wiesbaden.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The fact that my courses got cancelled was a pitty. I think I could've learned more by taking normal courses compared to the internships i did.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information page of Goethe University for exchange students was quite helpful. The document of the coordinate advisor is confusing, though. And for my case it was updated, as my advisor (Karen Hahn) did'nt have Copenhagen University beside her name.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did'nt recieve any assistance, which was okay, as I also had my german boyfriend to help me translate and understand official things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been nice with an event to meet fellow erasmus students from my department, but as i could understand there was not that many because of the new english master in biology.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it via WG-gesucht, which was good to use. When I found something there that was interesting I wrote a small bit about myself which I sended to the landlord (or potential roommate).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It depends of who you are, but I think it's nice to find something like a WG where you have a roommate and you get to know new people in another way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Actually, I don't really remember what I did there. I feel like most of the things happened through mobiliy online which it maybe did?

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
In terms of what?

I had a lot of help from my coordinate advisor Karen Hahn about my courses being cancelled and what I then could do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did it through my coordinate advisor Karen Hahn, but unfortunately they were cancelled due to few registrations.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That it's nice to get help from the coordinate advisor in the choise of courses as they might know if it's in english and if it meets your expectations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I did two internships instead of courses. I was nice in terms of getting an insight into the scientific work, but I think there has to be a planned schedule and goal for the praktikum for it to be nice and that you get the full out of it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two german language courses which were at bachelor level and the internships were at master level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I can't really answer that as I didn't take normal courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Two internships: One in ecotoxicoloy and one in botany
Two german language courses.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
It's nice to take a german language course as you learn how to talk in everyday situations which is helpful. It also gives an insight to the culture and you meet foreign students from other studies. 

Internships are also nice, but there needs to be a plan and a goal for the internship.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were cheaper than i expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of possibilities to di sports through Uni-Sport. They have a lot of difference things where you also have the possibility to meet german people and students from other countries.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I did badminton which was nice. 

I also participated in the Uni-choir which was also super cool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really like the Rheingau region where you have a lot of wineyards which are cool to do a hike in. Local festivals and markets are also super nice and happened oftenly in and around Frankfurt.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite okay I think it's not that different from at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participating in sports is cool to do, and also to go to the erasmus coordinated events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people generally are really nice and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
To do a german language course.
To participate in Uni-sport.
To be open to meet people that are different than you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: To be able to do normal courses or have a good plan for an internship.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To try and live in another country and be a part of another culture. It gives you another perspective on how you do things at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To have the courage to speak german.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
